claims.text: Removing Co from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi reduces local lattice distortion in equiatomic FeNiCrMn.
Removing Co alters the balance of solute–dislocation interactions.
The absence of Co lowers intrinsic lattice friction at room temperature.
The absence of Co enhances dislocation inertial effects at cryogenic temperatures.
The absence of Co reduces dynamic solute pinning at elevated temperatures.
Reduced lattice distortion can be quantified as a lower mean-square atomic displacement than in Co-containing alloys.
Lower lattice friction accentuates the role of inertial dislocation motion at low temperatures.
Dynamic solute pinning by Mn and Fe is less effective in Co-free FeNiCrMn than in Co-containing CoCrFeMnNi.
Phonon damping is reduced at cryogenic temperatures.
Reduced phonon damping and lower lattice friction enhance dislocation inertial motion.
Enhanced dislocation inertial motion produces a steeper cryogenic increase in CRSS.
At elevated temperatures, diffusion of Fe and Mn produces dynamic dislocation pinning associated with a Portevin–Le Chatelier effect.
The less-effective high-temperature pinning in FeNiCrMn produces milder CRSS enhancement than in CoCrFeMnNi.
The less-effective high-temperature pinning in FeNiCrMn produces less serrated flow than in CoCrFeMnNi.
Relative to CoCrFeMnNi, FeNiCrMn will show a sharper increase in CRSS when cooled below room temperature.
Below approximately 77 K, the increase in CRSS will become less steep because of dislocation inertia.
Above approximately 700 K, FeNiCrMn will have a smaller CRSS increment than CoCrFeMnNi.
Above approximately 700 K, FeNiCrMn will have less-pronounced serrated flow than CoCrFeMnNi.
Short-range order and magnetic interactions may alter the quantitative CRSS and serration differences between the alloys.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and mechanism attribute a steeper low-temperature CRSS increase to dislocation inertia, whereas the predicted outcome says dislocation inertia makes the CRSS increase less steep below approximately 77 K.

The intervention extends testing to approximately 9 K and the conditions discuss measuring inertial onset, but the stated applicability boundary is above an inertial cutoff near 60–77 K and the conditions exclude regimes dominated by extreme inertial dynamics.
